original_question: Let CT,S be the set of sequences of the form (∫ f · T^n g · S^n h dµ) as (X, X, µ, T, S) ranges over systems and f, g, h range over L∞(µ), and let CT be the subclass where T and S are powers of a single transformation. Must CT,S and CT actually coincide?
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the special-case open problem in Section 4.1 comparing the class of bicorrelation sequences coming from two commuting transformations with the subclass coming from powers of one transformation, and it asks for exact coincidence of the two classes rather than merely approximate coincidence.
missing_details: The paper’s ambient objects are probability-preserving systems: (X, X, µ) is a probability space, and T,S are commuting, invertible, measure-preserving transformations.

The sequences are bounded complex-valued correlation sequences a(n), not just arbitrary formal sequences; in Section 4.1 the multicorrelation sequences are defined on Z^ℓ, so here one should specify the index variable n (typically n in Z, or equivalently n in N for the averaging questions).
The functions should be quantified explicitly as f_0,f_1,f_2 in L∞(µ).
The definition of C_T should make precise what "powers of a single transformation" means: there exist an invertible measure-preserving transformation R and integers p,q such that T=R^p and S=R^q.
No ergodicity assumption is present in Problem 2; the classes range over all such systems.

The paper places this as a special case of the broader structural Problem 1 on multicorrelation sequences, so the intended scope is structural, not a neighboring convergence criterion from Section 4.2.

Immediately before Problem 2, the paper records a theorem showing that for ℓ=2 one already has coincidence only up to a negligible L^2-type error; the open problem asks for exact set equality, not equality modulo such errors.
refined_question: Let C_{T,S} be the collection of all bounded complex sequences a=(a(n))_{n in Z} of the form a(n)=∫_X f_0 · T^n f_1 · S^n f_2 dµ, where (X, X, µ) ranges over probability spaces, T and S range over commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of X, and f_0,f_1,f_2 range over L∞(µ). Let C_T be the subclass consisting of those sequences for which there exist an invertible measure-preserving transformation R and integers p,q such that T=R^p and S=R^q. Is it true that C_{T,S}=C_T?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation to your draft. In Section 4.1 the paper first defines multicorrelation sequences, then discusses the special case of linear bicorrelation sequences, then introduces the two classes C_{T,S} and C_T precisely to ask whether commuting transformations produce genuinely new sequences beyond those arising from powers of one transformation. The paper then states, verbatim in Problem 2, the exact question "Show that C_{T,S}=C_T." The neighboring unnumbered theorem explains that equality is already known only modulo a negligible error, so the paper’s intended sharpened question is exact equality of the classes, which your draft is aiming at.
